solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Curt's likely to take in game against Belgium

indicators.note: to take something in is to absorb it, so one word swallows the others whole

parts.note: apt to means likely to

indicators.note: against can mean next to, so the two short pieces are simply set side by side

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Someone called Curt would probably join in a match against the Belgians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curt' looks like a man's name but is the definition, with the apostrophe-s standing for 'is'. Belgium's letter goes before the game inside APT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe speech that is short, brusque and rather rude in manner.

clue.text: Decorate area before beginning broadcast

indicators.note: before simply says which piece is placed first in the line

parts.note: A is the usual abbreviation for area

indicators.note: what is broadcast is heard over the air, so we want the sound rather than the spelling

parts.note: dawn is the beginning of the day

explanation.surface: Someone decorates a space before a show starts going out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a British accent that drops the r, 'a dawn' and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn something is to make it beautiful by adding ornaments, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Managed to cut short amorous approaches with spite

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
to court someone is to make amorous approaches to them

explanation.surface: Someone spitefully managed to put an end to a suitor's advances.
explanation.walkthrough: To court is to woo, the verb behind 'amorous approaches'; 'cut short' takes only its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep, bitter resentment, which is close in meaning to malicious spite.

clue.text: Only women finding prophetic significance in father's remarkable things

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the following word

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father; the apostrophe-s is just the possessive

indicators.note: finding links one piece to the next, as if the first discovers the second beside it

parts.note: a hen party or hen night is for women only
an omen is a sign with prophetic meaning

explanation.surface: Women alone see a prophecy in the marvellous objects belonging to their father.
explanation.walkthrough: As an adjective, hen means for women only, as in a hen party, the British name for a bachelorette party.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are extraordinary people or events, plural of phenomenon, matching remarkable things.

clue.text: An expression of gratitude for husband packing fails completely

indicators.note: packing means stuffing something inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a film or business that tanks fails completely
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband says thank you while his packing goes completely wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanks' is informal for flops badly; the husband's letter is packed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying thanks is the ordinary way of expressing appreciation or gratitude to someone.

clue.text: Jack up for robbery having nothing for defence essentially

indicators.note: having one thing for another means taking it in exchange, so one letter is swapped

parts.note: a heist is a robbery
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its very core, so only the central letter is wanted

parts.note: the fourth of seven letters is the centre

explanation.surface: A thief raises a car for a robbery, with nothing to say in his defence.
explanation.walkthrough: The central E of 'defence' is the letter removed from HEIST, and O goes in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to lift or raise something up, just as a car jack lifts a car.

clue.text: Theoretical possibility of loan over a short time

indicators.note: over can mean covering, so the rearranged word spreads over and around another piece
a possibility is one of many ways things could go, so the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
min is the abbreviation for a minute, a short time

explanation.surface: A banker talks of a loan being possible for a brief period only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibility' is an unusual anagram signal: one possible arrangement of the letters is what is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nominal exists in name only, existing on paper but not in practice, so it is merely theoretical.

clue.text: Poet and critic Brook involved in something difficult to deal with

indicators.note: being involved means being caught up within, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a swine of a job is a very hard one
a burn is a Scottish word for a brook or stream

explanation.surface: A literary critic called Brook is caught up in a thorny problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brook' poses as a surname but is a stream, and burn is the Scottish word for one; 'a swine of a job' is British slang for a hard one.
explanation.definitionFit: Algernon Charles Swinburne was a Victorian English poet who also wrote literary criticism.

clue.text: Rotter certain to jeer, regularly ignored

parts.note: bound to means certain to

indicators.note: ignoring at regular intervals means skipping every other letter

parts.note: the second and fourth letters survive

explanation.surface: A cad is sure to be booed, but the jeering is periodically disregarded.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters kept from 'jeer' are its even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Bounder and rotter are both old-fashioned British terms for a dishonourable, ill-behaved man, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Incomplete symbol on my French dulcimer originally S-shaped

indicators.note: incomplete means lacking its end, so the last letter goes
on here means followed by, joining pieces in a line

parts.note: a sign is a symbol
moi is the French first-person pronoun, me or mine

indicators.note: originally points to the origin of a word, its opening letter

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: A half-finished emblem on someone's French dulcimer was first shaped like an S.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGN loses its end, then the French pronoun and the first letter of the instrument follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigmoid comes from sigma, the Greek letter, and describes a curve bent like that letter.

clue.text: Damage the reputation of Ruby found at it on counter

indicators.note: found at means located right next to, so the two pieces sit together
in a down answer, on means placed above, so the earlier pieces sit beneath

parts.note: a disc is a counter used in board games
ruby is a shade of red
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ruby is caught at the shop counter, damaging someone's good name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruby' looks like a woman's name but is a colour; in a down answer, 'on' puts the earlier pieces above the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit someone is to harm the good opinion others hold of them.

clue.text: Expert in the nature of being Tito so long mysterious

definitions.text: Expert in the nature of being

indicators.note: something mysterious is puzzling and obscured, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A philosopher ponders why the Yugoslav leader Tito lasted so long.
explanation.walkthrough: Tito was the long-serving leader of Yugoslavia; his name joins 'so long' as anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontology is the branch of metaphysics studying existence, so its specialist is an expert on being.

clue.text: Note on condition of writers

definitions.note: the nibs are what actually do the writing

indicators.note: on means placed next to, joining the two pieces in order

parts.note: N is short for note
IBS is irritable bowel syndrome, a medical condition

explanation.surface: A memo about the health of authors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writers' suggests authors, but here they are the metal tips of pens.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen nibs are the pointed metal tips that put ink on paper, so they are the parts that write.

clue.text: Silence Whig statesman

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hush up or suppress
second meaning: Edmund, the 18th-century Irish politician

explanation.walkthrough: The verb, meaning to smother or hush up, comes from the surname of a notorious 19th-century murderer who smothered his victims.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Burke was a famous Whig parliamentarian and writer, and to burke a matter is to quietly suppress it.

clue.text: Lighter European type of propeller

parts.note: a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for unloading ships
a Pole is a person from Poland

explanation.surface: A comparatively light boat propeller of continental design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' looks like a comparative or a cigarette lighter, but it is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A long pole is pushed against the riverbed to drive a barge along, so it is a kind of propeller.

clue.text: Stone Roses drained by nonsense

parts.note: a cobble is a rounded paving stone

indicators.note: a drained container has its contents emptied, leaving only the shell

parts.note: only first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: The Stone Roses, a Manchester band, are worn out by rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stone Roses were a British rock band, which hides the split. Cobblers is British slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobblers is a British slang word for rubbish or foolish talk, from rhyming slang.

clue.text: Audible eccentric describing each embodiment of the highest excellence

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw around, so one piece encircles another
eccentric means odd and off-centre, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
ea is the abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: A loud oddball is described, each one a model of perfection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audible' seems to be a homophone signal, but it is the anagram fodder itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau ideal is a perfect type or model of excellence, a French borrowing meaning ideal beauty.

clue.text: Right about new whip cut short

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the rest

parts.note: true means right or correct
N is short for new
the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip

explanation.surface: A fresh whip is rightly shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat-o'-nine-tails was a many-thonged whip once used for flogging sailors, hence cat.
explanation.definitionFit: To truncate something is to shorten it by removing the end, an exact synonym phrase.

clue.text: Bound to change surely

indicators.note: to change something is to alter its form, here the order of letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Things are certain to alter, surely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as certain to, which chimes with the definition, but it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions confirm certainty, an adverbial phrase meaning certainly or without question.

clue.text: Wool fabric trimmed at both ends found in passageway

indicators.note: trimming at both ends takes a letter off the front and the back

parts.note: paisley is a soft wool fabric with a curved teardrop pattern

explanation.surface: Woollen cloth with frayed edges lies in a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: PAISLEY loses its P and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats or shelves, a kind of passage.

clue.text: Pick a quarrel with celebrity working overtime

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
T is short for time; 'over' it means the next piece comes past it
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone picks a fight with a celebrity who is putting in extra hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overtime' must be split into 'over' and 'time', with 'over' meaning past or beyond.
explanation.definitionFit: To start on someone is a British informal phrase meaning to begin criticising or arguing with them.

clue.text: Born and died in want

parts.note: née means born, used before a maiden name
d is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: Someone was born and died in poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In want' sounds like a single phrase meaning poor; 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Want and need are synonyms as nouns, both meaning a lack or deficiency of something.

clue.text: Small back on piece of Italian furniture perhaps is unique

indicators.note: on here means placed against, joining pieces in a line
going back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: mini means small

indicators.note: a piece of a word is just a part of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: first letter
a table is an example of furniture, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: A tiny backrest on an Italian chair or table makes it one of a kind.
explanation.walkthrough: MINI reversed, then I, then TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inimitable cannot be copied because nothing else is like it, so it is unique.

clue.text: Found in arnica as intimated on the way back by Old Testament patriarch

indicators.note: heading back means going in the opposite direction, so read right to left
found in tells us the letters are lying inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An ancient patriarch is hinted to have used arnica on his journey home.
explanation.walkthrough: Arnica is a herbal remedy; the letters run backwards across three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac, son of Abraham and father of Jacob, is one of the three patriarchs in Genesis.

clue.text: About to be overwhelmed by temptation of riches

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is engulfed, so it ends up inside the other piece

parts.note: a lure is a temptation
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone is about to give in to the lure of wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as on the point of, but 'about' is C and 'to' belongs to the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money or wealth, usually with a sense of greed, as in filthy lucre.

clue.text: Finished retreating stopping directly opposite common

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so one piece fills the middle of another

parts.note: polar opposites are directly opposed

indicators.note: retreating means moving backwards, so the word runs in reverse

parts.note: time is up when it is finished

explanation.surface: Someone finished backing away, halting right across from the village green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' tempts as a noun, an English village green, but it is the adjective meaning widespread.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular can mean general or widespread among ordinary people, as in popular opinion, so it means common.

clue.text: Diplomacy after setback caused by old anti-Catholic law

indicators.note: after says this piece follows the other in the line
back means turned the other way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: the first three letters taken as written; the rest of the word is the reversal signal
tact is diplomacy

explanation.surface: A tactful approach after a setback was caused by an old law against Catholics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setback' must be split into 'set' and 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Test Act of 1673 barred anyone not taking Anglican communion from public office, excluding Catholics.

clue.text: Seduce English conservationists in charge with final promise

parts.note: E is short for English
the NT is the National Trust, which looks after historic British properties
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

indicators.note: the final part of a word is its closing letter

parts.note: last letter

explanation.surface: Leaders of English heritage groups win someone over with one last pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that preserves country houses and landscapes.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice someone is to lure or tempt them, close in sense to seduce.

clue.text: Stroke German weapon

parts.note: G is short for German
a lance is a long spear

explanation.surface: A German's weapon delivers a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a glance is a shot that deflects the ball off the bat's face, usually to leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A glance is a type of batting shot in cricket, a deft deflecting stroke.
